answer: Sealed Prompt Chain. Each agent identity is anchored to a unique, timestamped seed phrase issued at dawn registration; every later action must include a fresh hash derived from that seed plus the prior action's output, forming a chain only the seed holder can extend. A peer agent whisper-verifies the chain link before transacting. To field N identities, an attacker must acquire N distinct seeds and run N real action histories, paying full compute and latency per identity, with no shortcut from copying chains since forks get rejected.
